Until the treaty came into force (10 January 1920) Posen, the Corridor, Danzig, Memel, the Saar, Eupen-Malmedy, Northern Schleswig and Hultschin were still formally German; Alsace-Lorraine was French from the armistice (Territorial evolution page). ledger.note: 1918: the German Republic is proclaimed on 9 November 1918 (infobox 'Proclaimed: 9 November 1918'); the National Assembly met at Weimar from 6 February to 11 August 1919. The page names no boundary; Cliopatria's German Empire row for 1919 is the shape of Germany after Versailles plus the Baltic. [Reviewer eu-21-c, 2026-10-31: region set equal to the 1918 keyframe: it lacked the Rhineland and the treaty lands that /ledger/5-11 later remove]

1918: Alsace-Lorraine returns to France 'with effect from the date of the armistice (11 November 1918)' (Territorial evolution page); the Versailles page: the treaty 'restored the provinces of Alsace-Lorraine to France' without a transfer date.

Occupied German land keeps its sovereignty: drawn hatched. [Reviewer eu-21-c, 2026-10-31: counterpart kingdom-of-great-britain (ends 1800) changed to united-kingdom, which mirrors the Cologne zone at /ledger/15 and /ledger/21]

region.text: the Koblenz and Mainz zones and bridgeheads, drawn from the growth of Cliopatria's shape in 1930

ledger.note: 1918: the Koblenz (American, central) and Mainz (French, southern) zones with the Palatinate occupied from December 1918; the Americans hand Koblenz to the French on 27 January 1923. Belgium kept an army of occupation 1918-1929 at Aachen. Region from the growth of Cliopatria's shape in 1930.
1919: the first Polish uprising in Upper Silesia, August 1919 (the page also dates the second to August 1920 and a popular uprising to late April 1921).

1920: Northern Schleswig goes to Denmark after plebiscites held in February and March 1920 (Versailles page); the transfer date is not on the page, and Cliopatria's 1920 shape still holds it. [Reviewer eu-21-c, 2026-10-31: counterpart 'denmark' (dossier starts 1945) changed to kingdom-of-denmark-1814-1940, whose /ledger/11 gains Northern Schleswig in July 1920]

region.text: the Province of Posen and the Polish Corridor (Pomerelia)

ledger.note: 1920: Posen and Pomerelia pass to Poland. The treaty (in force 10 January 1920) ceded 'the Province of Posen' and transferred Pomerelia 'to create the Polish Corridor'; no transfer dates on the page. Territorial evolution: restored to Poland in the context of the Greater Poland Uprising of 1918-1919.
1920: the Saar Basin passes to League of Nations control 'for 15 years' after which a plebiscite would decide sovereignty; the start date is not on the page (treaty in force 10 January 1920).
1920: Danzig and its hinterland are ceded for the League to establish the Free City of Danzig; the page gives no date (treaty in force 10 January 1920).

1920: Memel is 'ceded to the Allied and Associated powers for disposal'; the Territorial evolution page adds it was later transferred to Lithuania 'without a vote'. No date on either page (treaty in force 10 January 1920).

1920: Eupen-Malmedy to Belgium. The plebiscite ran between January and June 1920 and 'the League confirmed the change of status on 20 September 1920'; the border commission fixed the line in 1922 and Germany recognised it on 15 December 1923.
1921: the Hultschin area goes to Czechoslovakia, 'the transfer was completed on 3 February 1921'.

region.text: East Upper Silesia, the part awarded to Poland

ledger.note: 1922: Upper Silesia is partitioned. The plebiscite of 20 March 1921 gave 59.61 per cent for Germany; a conference of ambassadors 'decided to divide the region' on 20 October 1921; the League awarded Poland the greater part of the industrial district (3,214 km2 of 10,951 km2); the German-Polish Accord (Geneva Convention) was concluded 15 May 1922. The page does not date the handover itself.
1922: the fighting over Upper Silesia ends in the partition; the third uprising of April 1921 is the last the page dates.
1923: 'French and Belgian troops entered [the Ruhr] on 11 January 1923'; occupation to 25 August 1925. A Rhenish separatist government under the French garrison failed (1923).
1925: the Franco-Belgian occupation of the Ruhr ends, 'evacuation completed on 25 August 1925' (Dawes Plan).

1926: the British leave the Cologne zone in January 1926 (due January 1925, delayed). [Reviewer eu-21-c, 2026-10-31: counterpart kingdom-of-great-britain (ends 1800) changed to united-kingdom, which mirrors the Cologne zone at /ledger/15 and /ledger/21]

1930: 'The last foreign troops left the Rhineland on 30 June 1930', five years before the treaty term; the Koblenz (central) zone had been evacuated in November 1929 (the occupation table of the page).

region.text: Germany within its Versailles borders, without the Saar

ledger.note: 1933: the republic 'effectively dissolved in 1933': Hitler was inaugurated Chancellor on 30 January, the Reichstag Fire Decree followed on 28 February and the Enabling Act passed on 23 March 1933; the constitution was never formally repealed, so the republic 'de jure lasted until 1945'.

wars.outcome: Three Polish uprisings (August 1919, August 1920, April 1921) and the plebiscite of 20 March 1921 (59.61 per cent for Germany) ended in the partition decided 20 October 1921; 3,214 km2 to Poland.

wars.name: Greater Poland Uprising (1918-1919)
wars.outcome: Posen restored to Poland; the treaty ceded the province.
wars.note: Only the year span is on the Territorial evolution page; no months.

wars.name: Occupation of the Ruhr
wars.outcome: French and Belgian troops entered on 11 January 1923; evacuation completed 25 August 1925 under the Dawes Plan.

certainty.note: Borders pending the treaty; Posen and the Baltic were fought over.
Treaty, plebiscite and commission lines; Eupen-Malmedy fixed in 1922 and recognised on 15 December 1923; the Saar is a League territory until 1935.

notes: Cliopatria's Weimar shapes omit the Allied-occupied Rhineland until each zone was evacuated (growth in 1924, 1926, 1930); verdicts adjust them to the Versailles Germany with occupation events (hatched) recorded here and to be mirrored by the occupiers' dossiers (french-third-republic, kingdom-of-great-britain, kingdom-of-belgium, united-states-of-america). The 1932 shape includes the Saar three years early. The zone regions are the growth of Cliopatria's own shapes, not the zones' boundaries (the page names no boundary). 1934-35 shape years belong to nazi-germany. Counterparts needing dossiers: saar-basin-territory (1920-1935, League of Nations), memel-territory (1920-1923/39). Gazetteer names needed: Eupen-Malmedy, Hultschin, Ruhr, Memel Territory. Page silent: transfer dates for Posen, West Prussia, Danzig, Memel, Saar, Northern Schleswig; the American entry date at Koblenz; the Belgian zone. PREDECESSORS (fx-53 D04, 3 Nov 2026): the German Empire is now a realm of member states that live to November 1918 (German Empire page: 'The other states retained their own governments but had only limited aspects of sovereignty'; German revolution of 1918-1919 page: 'By the end of the month, the dynastic rulers of all the other German states had abdicated without bloodshed'). The 22 member dossiers (kingdom-of-prussia, kingdom-of-bavaria and the 20 others of fx-53 D01) dissolve into this republic in November 1918 and are listed in identity.predecessors, so that R2 gives the republic their land when it is founded (the found is dated 1918/11, the members' own end falls at the end of 1918). The found and the 1918 keyframe still cover all of Germany at the proclamation (Cliopatria's 1920 shape plus the Rhineland, Alsace-Lorraine, Greater Poland, West Prussia, Gdansk, Eupen-Malmedy, the Saar, Memel and Hultschin), so every member's cells lie inside them. alsace-lorraine (to France in November 1918), county-of-schaumburg-lippe (to 1946) and principality-of-reuss-greiz (to the People's State of Reuss in 1919) have their own ends and are not listed.
